title: The Magpie of the Steaming Terraces
story: The village of Kettlespout keeps its winter savings — 480 moonstone shards — in a basket beside the hot springs. Brumbleflint the Geyser Grackle swooped down, snatched five-eighths of the whole basket, and hid the loot in his nest of steam. Mr 6 climbed the terraces and out-riddled the bird so thoroughly that Brumbleflint sheepishly gave back one quarter of everything he had taken.
question: After the grackle takes five-eighths of the 480 shards and then returns 25% of what he took, how many moonstone shards do the villagers have?
solution: The bird took 480 x 5/8 = 300 shards, so the village still held 480 - 300 = 180 shards.
He gave back 25% of 300, which is 300 x 0.25 = 75 shards.
praise: Finding five-eighths of 480 was the hard part and you got the shape of it — the last step was adding the returned quarter back onto what the village kept.
hint: First figure out how many shards stayed home, then work out a quarter of the stolen pile and add it on.
victory: Brumbleflint dropped the shards back with a grumpy squawk, then asked if Mr 6 could teach him fractions so he'd never be out-counted again. Mr 6 said yes — and charged one shiny shard as tuition.
imagePrompt: A big iridescent grackle perched on a nest of glittering moonstone shards atop steaming mineral terraces at sunrise, while a small knightly numeral 6 in a blue cape holds up a counting slate and the bird tilts its head in defeat.
